column1: # Glottography language-area datasets, one row per CLDF languages.csv.
# Adding a dataset is adding a row here. Nothing in the code names a dataset.
# These are the small index files, not the polygons. Each row's languages.csv
# lists which Glottocodes the dataset draws, which geojson file holds each one
# (Speaker_Area) and which features (Feature_IDs). Total about 2.4 MB, against
# roughly 400 MB for the geojson, so coverage can be answered without them.
# All Glottography datasets are CC BY 4.0. Re-check before launch, per dataset.
# kind, and why it decides which dataset wins:
#   language-area   contemporary attested speech areas, the ones we want
#   historical-area attested but a dated snapshot, Grierson 1903, Wurm 1981
#   country-shape   national outlines, right for a political standard only
#   reconstructed   ancestral ranges inferred from phylogenetics or archaeology
# reconstructed ranks LAST, below even country outlines. DiACL's Yiddish is a blob
# in eastern Poland, the pre-war heartland, which is not where Yiddish is spoken
# now. A modern border is closer to the truth than an ancestral range for a game
# that asks where a language is spoken today. Any entry that still lands on
# reconstructed or country-shape data is flagged for review in footprints.geojson.
